report:
Reviewed the entire coordinates claim, all three ordinary implementation entries (compile::prepare, annotations::parse, observe::collect), their whole-file context, and the complete three-test association set. There are no TODO/N/A entries or deferrals.

Evaluated source and no independent dedenting: compile_test! forwards its source expression as a value to source(), which copies AsRef<str> into the fixture map. validate_files clones source without whitespace transformation; prepare parses and writes those same strings. This handles indoc! as an already evaluated expression rather than special runner syntax. evaluated_source_retains_blank_lines_indentation_and_unicode supplies an intentional leading newline and indentation and asserts both physical diagnostic line 2 and exact indentation on lines 2 and 3; independent trimming or dedenting would invalidate these assertions.

Line coordinates include annotation lines: annotations::parse uses tree-sitter row positions on the unchanged string, source.split('\n'), and target + 1. Annotation-only lines are excluded as targets, not removed from coordinate accounting. inline_stacked_and_blank_lines_use_one_rule asserts [2, 2, 2, 6] across inline, stacked, blank, and ordinary-comment lines, catching renumbering that discards annotation lines. Its explicit actual-tab fixture asserts rejection containing tabs, matching parse's source.contains('\t') guard over the entire supplied source.

Type selection ignores horizontal alignment and Unicode width: observe::walk_expr derives row.line by counting newline bytes before the source span; collect selects solely by file and line, not a column. The marker carries no column after target selection. unicode_and_indentation_do_not_change_line_type_selection supplies indented source with the multibyte café identifier and a far-right inline marker; its exact observation snapshot requires both the true literal and containing block with bool types. That meaningfully rules out selecting only an expression horizontally aligned with the marker or losing expressions because of byte/character width confusion. Relative spans and source retrieval are upstream compiler inputs; the coordinate selection and preservation decisions being reviewed reside in the already associated files. No additional implementation association is necessary for this claim.

Source review found all requirements implemented and adequately asserted. Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib inline_stacked_and_blank_lines_use_one_rule; cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib evaluated_source_retains_blank_lines_indentation_and_unicode; and cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test compile_tests unicode_and_indentation_do_not_change_line_type_selection. Each ran its one selected test successfully. Existing compiler warnings appeared. No Rust files or test expectations were modified. The review-policy document was additionally captured using review read.
